summary: Christoph Harbsmeier specializes in sinology and linguistics. He studied at Merton College, Oxford, and completed his Ph.D. at Copenhagen. He taught at Universiti Sains Malaysia and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1980.

Christoph Kleine works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Marburg. He served as professor at the University of Munich (2004–2008) and became professor at Leipzig in 2008.

Christoph Theodosius Walther was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1720 and served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from around 1725 to 1739.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf worked in Indology and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate and habilitation at Vienna and studied at LSE. He was a professor at Osmania University before holding the Chair of Asian Anthropology at London (1951–1976).

Christoph-Ernst Hauri specialized in linguistics and Indology, earning his Ph.D. at Basel. He held posts at the universities of Geneva, Lausanne, Texas Health Science Center at Houston, and Queensland, and was a titular professor at Zurich (1988–1995).

Christophe Jaffrelot is a scholar of Indology who studied at Sciences Po under Jean Leca. He joined Sciences Po and the CNRS around 1991, and became Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology at King's College London around 2012.
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist. He has held academic posts as a research professor at KU Leuven (attested 2009) and as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (attested 2013).

Christopher Andreas Holmboe worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo and under Silvestre de Sacy and Caussin de Perceval. He served as lecturer and later professor at Oslo (1825–1876).

Christopher Braider earned his PhD from Trinity College Dublin. He held lecturer and associate professor appointments at Harvard University between 1983 and 1992, and became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder in 2003.

Christopher Byrne specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at McGill University under the supervision of Grace S. Fong, having also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates.
Christopher D. Emms works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, where he has studied under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.

Christopher G. Framarin works in philosophy and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a Ph.D. from the University of New Mexico, and joined the faculty at the University of Calgary.
Christopher Hatchell is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Virginia, where he studied under academic mentor David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, later joining the faculty at Indiana University.

Christopher Isherwood was a writer and scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Corpus Christi College and King's College London, studied under Swami Prabhavananda, and taught at California State University, Los Angeles (1959–1962).

Christopher Ives specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He was an assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound from 1987 to 1993 and later served as professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College.

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University, earning his PhD under James A. Benn.
Christopher Kelley is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple specializes in Indology and religious studies. He was a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions and later became Doshi Professor of Indic and Comparative Theology at Loyola Marymount University.

Christopher L. Diamond works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at SOAS and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Washington under Heidi R. M. Pauwels, later teaching at Puget Sound and Wisconsin-Madison in 2019.
